posts.body_html:
Interesting. Now after reading through the dialogue here I understand why the tea I've harvested from my home grown plants has been so smooth and not tannic at all. My tea seedlings are mostly little leaf types (of open pollinated mixed ancestry) which means they're dominantly the less tannic Camellia sinensis var. sinensis genetics rather than C. sinensis var. assamica.  I actually crave tannic teas sometimes, so maybe I should make some custom blends with Camellia and Aronia.  Lol...

I provided tea for a tea party my sister hosted this past summer and she said my tea (which I had harvested  and processed as a light black tea) reminded her of one she had tasted while traveling somewhere one time and had never been able to find anywhere else.  I'm looking forward to when I can have larger harvests in coming years! 

Regarding growing tea, I've found that it can grow pretty slow if not fertilized, but a nitrogen dominant fertilizer can really help it push growth at a respectable rate which means more frequent harvest of tender tips.
